clue.text: Direct attention to other facts — at 15?

definitions.text: Direct attention to other facts — at 15?

parts.words: Direct attention to other facts — at 15?
parts.note: pointing a reader on to related material elsewhere, with a hint that clue 15 (the crucifix, a rood) supplies the first half of the compound

explanation.surface: An instruction to point the reader to further information, with a query about where to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 across is ROOD, a crucifix, i.e. a CROSS; to direct attention elsewhere is to REFER, so the hint at 15 gives the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct a reader from one passage to related information elsewhere in a text is exactly this indexing practice.

clue.text: Girl with it finds fruit

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A girl who is trendy discovers some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bright red seed pod of a wild rose bush is a fruit, used for syrups and teas.

clue.text: Irishman seats daughter in big chair

indicators.note: to seat someone is to place them within, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: Sean is a typical Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irish father settles his daughter in a large armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair was an enclosed seat carried on poles, a grand chair for one passenger.

clue.text: Get radar working with some industry

indicators.note: letters that are working are being put to new use, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting radar into operation alongside a certain business.
explanation.walkthrough: The rag trade is a British informal name for the clothing and fashion business.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal term for the clothing manufacturing business, one particular industry.

clue.text: As this answer will be written throughout

definitions.text: As this answer will be written throughout

parts.words: As this answer will be written throughout
parts.note: a down entry is written entirely vertically, from its first square at the head of the grid to its last at the foot

explanation.surface: A remark about how this solution is to be entered in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a 15-letter down light, so it runs the full height of the grid, describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means entirely or completely, and literally describes a down entry spanning the whole grid.

clue.text: Our airmen flew without women to offer as prize

parts.note: the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force, our airmen from a British setter's view

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the word beside it

explanation.surface: British pilots took to the air with no women aboard, offering something as a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes W from FLEW, leaving FLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold a lottery for an item is to offer it as a prize to the holder of the drawn ticket.

clue.text: Low station

explanation.definitionFit: Base means morally low, and is also a station such as a military camp.

clue.text: Famed surgeon in bed with burns

indicators.note: in places the surgeon inside the bed

parts.note: taken as written
Joseph Lister was the pioneering surgeon of antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A celebrated surgeon is laid up in bed suffering from burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin covered with fluid-filled swellings, as after burning, is described this way.

clue.text: Soho Pam worked as a cleaner

indicators.note: worked means manipulated or kneaded, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Pam from Soho took a job as a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid soap for washing hair or carpets is a cleaning product.

clue.text: FT compilers editor worked unfairly

parts.note: the setters of the Financial Times crossword refer to themselves as us

explanation.surface: The newspaper's setters say their editor treated them unfairly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have exploited someone for selfish ends is to have manipulated them unfairly.

clue.text: One in for odd conversion during brilliant Christian festival

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: gay in its older sense means bright and showy, brilliant

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the rearranged letters
a conversion changes form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone converts during a splendid religious holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brilliant' is in its archaic sense of bright and showy, not clever. 'conversion' makes OODFRD from the fodder; 'in' and 'during' are the two container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The Friday before Easter, commemorating the crucifixion, is a Christian holy day.

clue.text: Star gets black eye

definitions.meaning: something that shines brightly, such as a star
a bruised eye after a punch, in slang

explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant star gleams, and slang uses the same word for a bruised, darkened eye.

clue.text: Box on radio to classify communication network

indicators.note: heard on radio means spoken aloud, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: the box is British slang for television, the telly
to type is to classify by category

explanation.surface: A television heard on the radio helps to categorise a communication network.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleprinter system linking machines over wires formed a telegraphic communication network.

clue.text: Pies about to be thrown at unionist politicians with added enjoyment

indicators.note: thrown means flung about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: C, from circa, means about
the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: Pies are about to be hurled at Ulster politicians, making things more fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be thrown' shuffles PIES plus C into SPICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made livelier or more exciting has had extra zest added to it.

clue.text: Worry about pet in case of bullets

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: care is worry or anxiety
to pet is to stroke or touch

explanation.surface: Anxious about a pet kept in an ammunition box.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche was historically a paper cartridge or box holding a soldier's ammunition.

clue.text: Crucifix seen where marsupial died

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a marsupial

explanation.surface: A crucifix marks the spot where a kangaroo perished.
explanation.definitionFit: A large crucifix set above a church screen is the traditional name for a cross.

clue.text: She hates collapse in cricket series

indicators.note: a collapse breaks something down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman despises a batting collapse during a cricket series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series played between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous trophy contested between England and Australia names this Test series.

clue.text: Sailor coming about succeeded tyrant

indicators.note: coming about means going round, so the sailor surrounds the letter

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman turning his ship after the despot took over.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian emperor wielded absolute power, so the title stands for an autocratic ruler.

clue.text: Resin down there in bag

indicators.note: in places the underworld inside the bag

parts.note: a sac is a pouch or bag
hell is traditionally below, down there

explanation.surface: Some resin kept below ground in a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A resin secreted by the lac insect is used for varnish, so it is a resin.

clue.text: Snake at work kept secret by Scotsman

indicators.note: by means next to, so the name follows

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
hid means kept secret
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A snake at work is concealed by a Scottish man.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoological word for snakes and snakelike creatures, from the Greek for serpent.

clue.text: So aliens are said to walk on with magus in play

definitions.text: So aliens are said to walk

indicators.note: in play means being moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Aliens supposedly walking on stage with a wise man in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the popular saying that aliens walk among us.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular lore claims extraterrestrials live in our midst, completing that saying about aliens.

clue.text: Seen to unite after struggle

indicators.note: after means coming later, so the second word follows the first

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete
to wed is to unite in marriage

explanation.surface: Seen coming together after a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something looked at or observed has been seen.

clue.text: Child sent back into gully gives exhilarated cry

indicators.note: into means put inside, so the reversed piece goes within

parts.note: a geo is a narrow coastal gully or inlet, a Scottish word

indicators.note: sent back means reversed in direction

parts.note: a minor is a child in law

explanation.surface: A child thrown back into a ravine lets out a whoop.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroopers popularised the Apache leader's name as a whoop when jumping.

clue.text: Prize-winning author in forest

parts.note: at means in, as in at home
a wood is a forest

explanation.surface: An award-winning writer in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret, the Canadian novelist, has twice won the Booker Prize.

clue.text: Arabian Lawrence in conflict with something damp

indicators.note: in places the initials inside the conflict

parts.note: war is conflict
T. E. Lawrence was Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia fights against something wet.
explanation.definitionFit: The liquid of rivers and rain is the archetypal wet substance.

clue.text: Depressing to look upon Scots regiment

parts.note: bleak, gloomy and dismal in mood
to observe or keep an eye on

explanation.surface: It's gloomy to observe a Scottish military unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Black Watch is a famous Highland regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous Highland infantry unit is a regiment of the British Army.

clue.text: Takeaway place in Africa

definitions.meaning: food bought for eating elsewhere, as said when ordering
a West African country between Ghana and Benin

explanation.definitionFit: A takeaway order is said to be for carrying out, and the West African republic shares the spelling.

clue.text: Muslims here besieged are without cold water

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the word surrounds the letter

parts.note: C marks the cold water tap

explanation.surface: Besieged Muslims have no cold water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Crusaders besieged the Muslim garrison of this port in present-day Israel from 1189 to 1191. 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: The port city in present-day Israel held by Saladin's garrison was besieged by Crusaders.

clue.text: Question came up after lunatic sent back flower

indicators.note: after means following, so the question and rising follow
sent back means reversed in direction

parts.note: mad means lunatic
to ask is to question
rose means came up

explanation.surface: A question arose after a madman was returned, about a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant pink rose variety grown for attar of roses is a flower.
